title: Add a comment on its own line
instruction: Add **# This program prints numbers** on line 1.
starter_code:
# Add a comment on this line
print(10)
print(20)
solution_code:
# This program prints numbers
print(10)
print(20)
test_suite:
import io, sys
import re

def test_prints_numbers():
    captured = io.StringIO()
    sys.stdout = captured
    exec(open("exercise.py").read())
    sys.stdout = sys.__stdout__
    output = captured.getvalue()
    assert output == '10\n20\n'

def test_has_comment_on_own_line():
    with open("exercise.py") as f:
        code = f.read()
    assert '# This program prints numbers' in code

title: Add an inline comment
instruction: Add an inline comment at the end of print().
test_suite:
import io, sys
import re

def test_prints_greeting_inline():
    captured = io.StringIO()
    sys.stdout = captured
    exec(open("exercise.py").read())
    sys.stdout = sys.__stdout__
    output = captured.getvalue()
    assert output == 'Hi there!\n'

def test_has_inline_comment():
    with open("exercise.py") as f:
        code = f.read()
    h=False
    for l in code.split("\n"):
        s=l.strip()
        if '#' in s and not s.startswith('#'):
            h=True;break
    assert h

title: Comment out a line
instruction: Comment out the first print() so only the second runs.
starter_code:
print("This should not run")
print("This should run")
solution_code:
# print("This should not run")
print("This should run")
test_suite:
import io, sys
import re

def test_prints_second_line_only():
    captured = io.StringIO()
    sys.stdout = captured
    exec(open("exercise.py").read())
    sys.stdout = sys.__stdout__
    output = captured.getvalue()
    assert output == 'This should run\n'

def test_first_line_commented():
    with open("exercise.py") as f:
        code = f.read()
    first = code.strip().split("\n")[0].strip()
    assert first.startswith("#")
